original_question: Let G be a complete Hausdorff topological group such that for every nontrivial element g in G there exists an open normal subgroup N not containing g with soluble quotient G/N. Find useful characterizations of when G is isomorphic to the true prosoluble completion PS(Γ) of a residually soluble group Γ, and decide in particular how to tell whether G is isomorphic to PS(Γ) for some finitely generated group Γ or for some finitely presented group Γ.
target_in_paper: Introduction, item (iii): the open problem asking for "interesting characterizations" of complete Hausdorff topological groups G, separated by open normal subgroups with soluble quotients, that arise as true prosoluble completions, especially from finitely generated or finitely presented groups. ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely: it uses the exact topological hypothesis on G from Introduction (iii), focuses on the true prosoluble completion PS(Γ) rather than the usual prosoluble completion built from finite soluble quotients, and preserves the two specific existence questions for finitely generated and finitely presented Γ. ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))
missing_details: PS(Γ) should be defined explicitly, as the pro-S-completion attached to the family S of normal subgroups of Γ with soluble quotient; the paper later notes that this is also the completion coming from the derived-series family (D_n(Γ))_{n≥0}. ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))

To make the question fully stand-alone, Γ should be identified as an abstract/discrete group, while G is a complete Hausdorff topological group. The paper treats groups as abstract unless topological structure is explicitly specified. ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))

The paper phrases this as an open-ended request for "interesting characterizations" and asks "how can it be decided whether" such a G is isomorphic to PS(Γ); your wording "find"/"decide" is close, but it reads slightly more like a solved classification problem than the paper does. ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))

If one wants the finiteness subquestions to be exact, they should be stated as two separate existence problems: whether there exists a finitely generated Γ with G ≅ PS(Γ), and whether there exists a finitely presented Γ with G ≅ PS(Γ). ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))
refined_question: Find interesting characterizations of those complete Hausdorff topological groups G for which every nonidentity element g∈G is omitted by some open normal subgroup N◁G with soluble quotient G/N, and which arise as the true prosoluble completion PS(Γ) of a residually soluble discrete group Γ; in particular, how can one decide whether a given such G is isomorphic to PS(Γ) for some finitely generated Γ, and how can one decide whether it is isomorphic to PS(Γ) for some finitely presented Γ? ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, since the family of all normal subgroups with soluble quotients and the family (D_n(Γ))_{n≥0} from the derived series define the same procompletion, and procompletions are identified with inverse limits of the corresponding quotient system, ask for characterizations of those complete Hausdorff topological groups G with the above separation property that are isomorphic to lim←_n Γ/D_n(Γ) for some finitely generated discrete group Γ, or for some finitely presented discrete group Γ, where D_0(Γ)=Γ and D_{n+1}(Γ)=[D_n(Γ),D_n(Γ)]. ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))
justification: The draft is not aiming at the Grothendieck-type problem from Introduction (i) and Section 7, but at the separate third open problem in the Introduction. The match is nearly verbatim: the hypothesis on G and the finitely generated/finitely presented subquestions are exactly those of item (iii). The only nearby paper-explicit sharpening is to spell out what PS(Γ) means via Section 4.B and, if desired, to use the equivalent derived-series/inverse-limit formulation supplied by Sections 5.C-5.D together with 2.D. ([mat.univie.ac.at](https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~arjantseva/Abs/ahkJ.pdf))
